pairs.difference: A, the lasso: the rope is drawn as one even-width tube. The coil on the left is a fat solid ring, and the open loop on the right is a thin perfect circle, so the outline reads like a pair of spectacles rather than a coiled rope with a running noose. Solidity is 0.397, below every real card. B, the neckerchief: a puffy knotted cloth with two tapered tails and a clear neck opening. The swelling is in line with the real neck pillow and boxing gloves.
pairs.fix: Draw a coiled lariat: several separate overlapping loops stacked in a loose coil, with a wider open noose trailing off one side through a small knotted eye. Keep the rope thin with slight twists, and let the loose end hang naturally.

pairs.difference: B, the cowboy hat: the brim is one smooth slab. Its left half rolls up into a thick blob and its right tip flips up into a thin curl, so the two sides don't match. The crown is a soft lump with a vague pinch and no crisp crease. A, the jacket: puffy but keeps its parts in order, with collar, two sleeves with cuffs, pockets and a sash, the way real cards do.
pairs.fix: Draw a cowboy hat with a thin, even brim that curls up equally on both sides. Give the crown a sharp center crease and two front pinches, and add a narrow band at its base.

pairs.difference: B, the steam locomotive: the boiler is a stubby barrel barely longer than it is wide. The smokestack is oversized, the cab is a plain box, and the drive wheels are crowded under it, which gives toy proportions. The cowcatcher bars are thin, but the engine body reads short and squat. A, the roller coaster: thin rails and ladder ties stay thin, and the cars sit on the track in the right relation.
pairs.fix: Draw a 19th-century steam locomotive with a long horizontal boiler, about three times as long as it is tall, and a slim flared smokestack. Put a tall cab at the rear and a row of large spoked drive wheels joined by thin connecting rods along the boiler's length.

pairs.difference: A, the barrel: the silhouette is one smooth capsule. The iron hoops barely break the outline, there is no visible lip at the top rim, and the bulge runs evenly with no stave steps. corner_rate is 0.0 and solidity 0.982, both outside the real range. B, the treasure chest: an open lid, a box with metal corner caps, and spilling coins give a broken, many-part outline.
pairs.fix: Draw a wooden barrel whose top rim sticks up slightly above the lid, with iron hoops that stand out from the staves as distinct raised bands. Make the outline step in and out at each hoop.

pairs.difference: A: the open book has flat page blocks and a straight cover edge, partly cut off by the frame. B: the stone chess table has a planar slab top with crisp corners, a square pedestal and two stump stools. Both keep flat faces flat and have a believable part count. Nothing on my vector separates them.

A, the saguaro: a trunk of even width with two mirror-image arms. All three are smooth tubes with domed caps, sausage-like and with no ribs breaking the outline. The arms join at the same height on both sides. B, the popcorn cart: thin posts, a scalloped awning, a handle, spoked wheels and a bucket give a busy outline with correctly thin parts.
pairs.fix: Draw a saguaro cactus whose arms branch at different heights and have different lengths. Let the outline show shallow vertical ribs, and taper the trunk slightly toward the top.

pairs.difference: B, the sheriff star: a flat five-point star with ball tips. The points are uneven in length, and the ball knobs are large relative to the arms, so the outline is a toy-like star with oversized round knobs. A, the ring box: a soft rounded box with the lid open, in line with the soft forms on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw a six-point sheriff badge with slender, even-length points and small ball tips about a third of the arm's width at the base. Give it a thin raised rim on a flat badge plate.

pairs.difference: B, the covered wagon: the part count is wrong. It is a two-wheeled cart with a single long tongue. The canvas cover is short and sits on a shallow box, and the wheels are oversized for the bed, so it reads like a toy cart rather than a wagon. A, the dock and rowboat: the planks are planar, the hull is a believable boat shape, and the rope stays thin.
pairs.fix: Draw a covered wagon with four spoked wheels, smaller at the front and larger at the back. Give it a long, deep wooden bed, a tall canvas cover over evenly spaced arched hoops that runs the full length of the bed, and a front tongue with a driver's seat.

pairs.difference: A: the bird feeder has flat plank roof and floor, crisp corners and a thin hanging rope. B: the mojito glass has a straight tapered wall, a thin straw and mint leaves. Both keep flat parts flat and thin parts thin, so nothing on my vector separates them.

B, the saloon doors: the doors stand in a free-standing post-and-lintel frame with no wall. The posts are heavy square beams with block feet, and the two short door leaves float in the middle of the frame with uneven gaps. thin_share is 0.033, far above the real maximum of 0.004, and solidity is 0.606, below range. A, the sneakers: chunky soles and a consistent shoe outline, in line with real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw swinging saloon doors set into a doorway in a wooden wall. Make the two leaves chest-high and of equal width, hanging close together at the center from thin hinges on slim door jambs.

pairs.difference: A is the retro computer, identical to a REAL lesson card: boxy monitor, flat keyboard, mouse with a thin cable. B, the saddle: a stubby horn, a swollen seat, and side fenders reduced to flat slabs. The stirrups are thick rounded loops, too heavy for the strap that holds them, and the saddle is draped over a fence rail with no saddle tree showing.
pairs.fix: Draw a western saddle with a tall slim horn and a high rounded back cantle. Make the fenders long leather flaps hanging down to the stirrups, and the stirrups narrow wooden loops on thin straps.

pairs.difference: B, the cowboy boot: the shaft is very tall and narrow, roughly twice the height of the foot. The foot is short with a long, flat, pointed toe, so the boot looks stretched upward, and the spur is a small afterthought at the heel. A, the graduation cap: a flat square board with a crisp corner, a skullcap with a rounded band, and a thin cord and tassel. Its proportions are true.
pairs.fix: Draw a cowboy boot whose shaft is about as tall as the foot is long, with a scalloped top edge. Give it a slightly pointed toe, an angled stacked heel, and a spur with a clear star rowel on a strap around the heel.

pattern: The generated western cards keep getting the object's structure wrong; the rendering isn't what gives them away. Proportions go toy-like: a stubby locomotive boiler, a boot shaft stretched far above the foot, wheels too big for a short cart bed. Parts are missing or rearranged: a two-wheeled 'covered wagon', a free-standing saloon door frame with no wall, a lasso drawn as two rings. Silhouettes are smoothed into one even mass where real objects break the outline: hoops on the barrel, ribs and branch heights on the cactus, a crease in the hat crown. Thin parts turn into sausage tubes or heavy beams. Solidity and thin_share often fall outside the real range on exactly these cards.
